title: DOISST v2.1 input steps add a false -0.22 to -0.27 W m-2 per decade to the 2001-2022 TOA trend in a CAM4 Green's function; the 1982-2022 feedback is robust (60S-60N)
abstract: Question: NOAA DOISST v2.1 has mean steps at satellite-input changes, and NOAA OI SST v2 (the post-1981 source of the AMIPII forcing) has a cold step in mid-2018. How much do these artifacts change the TOA radiation trend and the feedback parameter (lambda) that a Green's function (GF) calculates from the observed SST pattern? Approach: we applied the CAM4 radiative-feedback GF of Dong et al. (2019) to monthly anomalies of 12 SST versions on 5-degree boxes (60S-60N ice-free; HadISST1 elsewhere for all versions). The versions are three in situ products, ESA SST CCI v3.0.1, HadISST1, DOISST with and without its input steps, OI v2, PCMDI-AMIP 1.1.9 and OI v2 without its 2018 step. We used paired 24-month block-bootstrap intervals, step signatures, kernel components, 20-year windows, SST# and 96 GTMBA moorings. Results: the 1982-2022 lambda is robust (all versions -3.31 to -3.01 W m-2 K-1; DOISST minus in situ -0.07, interval -0.23 to +0.08). For 2001-2022, DOISST adds a false TOA trend of -0.27 W m-2 per decade (-0.33 to -0.21) against the in situ mean and -0.22 (-0.29 to -0.16) against CCI; removing the steps reduces it to -0.05 to +0.01. Each warm DOISST step (2005, 2020) acts like a uniform 0.08-0.10 K warming with a TOA signature of -0.23 to -0.37 W m-2. The error is in the Indo-Pacific warm pool; at 30 west Pacific moorings DOISST minus buoy SST rises by +0.090 C per decade in 2001-2022, and +0.007 to +0.020 with the steps removed. The 2001-2022 lambda depends more on the reference type: in situ -2.35 to -2.16, CCI -2.71, HadISST1 -2.60, corrected DOISST -2.61 to -2.70, DOISST -2.89. Thus about 0.2-0.3 of the DOISST difference is step artifact. DOISST halves the post-2000 weakening of the pattern effect (+0.77 against +1.39); half of this is step artifact. PCMDI-AMIP 1.1.9 equals OI v2 in the mask and contains the 2018 step (-0.14 C at 40-60S), which makes its 2001-2022 lambda 0.15-0.38 more negative. Limitations: one GF (CAM4) and a linear method; absolute lambda values are model-dependent; in situ and satellite references disagree by about 0.4 in the 2001-2022 lambda; the correction size is uncertain.

display.caption: Feedback lambda = trend(R)/trend(T) from the CAM4 Green's function for 12 SST versions, 1982-2022 (a) and 2001-2022 (b), with block-bootstrap 95% intervals (grey band: in situ range). (c, d) Error of the GF TOA trend against the in situ mean (filled) and against ESA CCI (open), paired intervals. DOISST (orange) has a TOA-trend error of -0.22 to -0.27 W m-2 per decade in 2001-2022; with the steps removed the error is near zero.

2001-2022 SST trend differences and their TOA effect: (a) CCI minus in situ mean; (b) in situ mean trend; (c) DOISST minus in situ mean and (d) its GF-weighted TOA effect, which is concentrated in the Indo-Pacific warm pool; (e, f) the same with the DOISST steps removed.

(a) lambda in moving 20-year windows: all versions show less negative feedback after 2000, but DOISST shows about half of the in situ change. (b) Trend of product minus mooring SST, 2001-2022, at GTMBA moorings: DOISST warms too fast in the west Pacific (+0.09 C per decade); the step-corrected versions do not.
